target_customer: Renters (free) and brokers/property managers who pay to promote listings
problem: Craigslist-style rental search is time-consuming and full of spam and bait-and-switch listings.
business_model: Marketplace; listing and promotion fees from brokers and property managers

founders.name: Lee C. Lin
founders.background_notes: Former programmer with quantitative finance background who owned rental properties and built the site after finding Craigslist inefficient for tenant search.

competitors.name: Craigslist
competitors.what: Dominant free classified listings for NYC rentals, with spam and bait-and-switch problems

technical_complexity.rationale: Listing aggregation and ranking site built by two founders in nine months for about $20,000 of personal savings; ranking algorithm and broker feeds are moderate engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Relationships with large NYC brokers and listing supply help, but listings were also sourced from outside data providers and competitors like Craigslist and StreetEasy had large audiences.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found; RentHop remained independent and later criticized StreetEasy price increases (2017-2019 blog).

market_need_then: Company said New York apartment vacancy rose from 2.5% in 2006 to 2.9% (Reis) and that Craigslist spam frustrated users; RentHop reported $15,000 in revenue in its first month (company claim in early press).
outcome_analysis: RentHop was built cheaply by two founders, reached early revenue within a month of launch, and remains Active with 9 listed employees after more than a decade in NYC. Lin has described it as largely bootstrapped with a small strategic seed and angel money, so its survival reflects capital efficiency rather than venture scale; precise revenue, funding and market share were not found.
notes: Aggregators report total raised of $20K to $25K across up to 3 rounds, which looks unreliable and is not recorded as amounts. The seed round (2014, Two Sigma Ventures, Social Starts) comes from search summaries of aggregator pages; the RentHop blog page returned 403 and TAP-NY interview host did not resolve (network). Success factor capital_efficiency is inferred. Education for Lin comes from a search summary.
